result:
**Not ready to publish.** Three things need fixing.

**1. No affiliate disclosure.** This is an affiliate post with a link ("You can find it here"), but nothing tells the reader. The disclosure must come in plain words at the top, before the first link. For example: "This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through them, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you."

**2. No product label.** I can't tell whether Pebblebrook is Owned, Tried or Wishlist, and I won't assume ownership. Please confirm which it is. If Tried, the post should say how and for how long.

| Product | Label | Hands-on claims |
|---|---|---|
| Pebblebrook Tea Co. | **Not given** | "easiest to pause", "the tins are lovely", "I've tried four tea subscriptions this year" |

Until the label is confirmed, those hands-on claims can't stay. If it's Wishlist, all three get cut.

**3. Superlative with no basis.** "Easiest to pause" compares Pebblebrook with three other subscriptions the draft never names. The brand can back up "subscribers can pause or cancel any time", and that is the safe version. "Easiest" needs the writer's real comparison, such as the number of steps or clicks in each, or it should go.

**Smaller points**
- "I've tried four tea subscriptions this year" is an experience claim that only the writer can verify. Name the four or drop the count.
- "The tins are lovely" is vague. Say what you noticed, such as the size, the lid or the design, and only if you've handled one.
- The link text "here" tells the reader nothing. Use the product name.

**Suggested compliant version, pending your answers:**
> This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through them, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.
>
> [If Owned/Tried: state which Pebblebrook subscription you used and for how long.] Pebblebrook subscribers can pause or cancel any time. [Add what you actually did to pause, and how many steps it took.] [Add one specific detail about the tin.] [Pebblebrook Tea Co. subscription](link)

